AX8052                                                          Performance
                                                                  The AX8052 core employs a pipelined architecture that
  The AX8052 core is fully compatible with the MCS-51
instruction set. Standard 803x/805x assembler and               greatly increases its instruction throughput over the standard
compilers can be used to develop software. The peripherals      8052 architecture. Instead of using 12, 24 or 48 clock cycles
however are vastly improved and therefore not compatible        to execute instructions, AX8052 requires between 1 and 11
with other 8051/8052 implementations.                           clock cycles depending on instructions. 90% of the
                                                                instructions are executed between 1 and 4 clock cycles.

PROGRAM BRANCHING

ACALL addr11         Absolute subroutine call

LCALL addr16         Long subroutine call

RET                  Return from subroutine

RETI                 Return from interrupt

AJMP addr11          Absolute jump

LJMP addr16          Long jump

SJMP rel             Short jump (relative addr)

JMP @A+DPTR          Jump indirect relative to the DPTR

JZ rel               Jump if Accumulator is zero

JNZ rel              Jump if Accumulator is not zero

CJNE A, direct, rel  Compare direct byte to ACC and jump if not equal

CJNE A, #data, rel   Compare immediate to ACC and jump if not equal

CJNE Rn, #data, rel  Compare immediate to register and jump if not equal

CJNE @Ri, #data, rel Compare immediate to indirect and jump if not equal

DJNZ Rn, rel         Decrement register and jump if not zero

DJNZ direct, rel     Decrement direct byte and jump if not zero

NOP                  No Operation

Data Memory                                                      Register Banks
  The AX8052 has 256 bytes of data memory mapping                  The AX8052 uses 8 "R" registers (locations 0x00 through

called IRAM (internal data) or SFR (Special Function             0x1F) which are used in many instructions. These "R"
Register) depending on the addressing mode used and the          registers are numbered from 0 through 7 (R0, R1, R2, R3,
address space access. The memory space goes from 0x00 to         R4, R5, R6, R7) and are generally used to assist in
0xFF.                                                            manipulating values and moving data from one memory
                                                                 location to another. The microcontroller has 4 distinct
  The lower 128 bytes of data memory are used for general        register banks and only one of these banks may be enabled
purpose registers, bits and scratch pad memory. Either direct    at a time. When the CPU is first booted up, register bank 0
or indirect addressing may be used to access the lower           is used by default. However, your program may instruct the
128 bytes of data memory:                                        CPU to use one of the alternate register banks; i.e., register
                                                                 bank 1, 2 or 3. In this case, R4 (for example) will no longer
· Location 0x00 Through 0x1F are Addressable as Four             be the same as internal RAM address 04h. Two bits in the
                                                                 Program Status Word (PSW), RS0 (PSW.3) and RS1
   Banks of General Purpose Registers, Each Bank                 (PSW.4), select the active register bank.
   Consisting of Eight Byte-Wide Registers.
                                                                   Indirect addressing mode uses registers R0 and R1 as
· The Next 16 bytes Locations 0x20 Through 0x2F May              index registers. The AX8052 has a directly accessible image
                                                                 of the active R0 and R1, speeding up indirect accesses.
   Either be Addressed as Bytes or as 128 bit Locations          Doing so, the core does not need to read R0 or R1 in IRAM
   Accessible with the Direct Addressing Mode.                   before doing an indirect access. Each time the active R0 or
                                                                 R1 register is changed, or when RS0 and/or RS1 is modified,
  The upper 128 bytes region represents the upper part of        the core updates the R0 and R1 images.
internal data memory and the SFR. They are physically
separated and are accessible through different addressing
modes:

AND9349/D

Interrupts                                                        Interrupt Vectors
  AX8052 includes an interrupt system supporting a total of
                                                                  Table 3. INTERRUPT VECTORS
22 interrupt sources with 2 priority levels.
  If interrupts are enabled for the source, an interrupt          Address                      Vector

request is generated when the interrupt input line is             0x0000 Reset
triggered. As soon as execution of the current instruction is
complete, the CPU generates an LCALL to a predetermined           0x0003 External 0 Interrupt
address to begin execution of an interrupt service routine
(ISR). Each ISR must end with an RETI instruction which           0x000B Wakeup Timer Interrupt
returns program execution to the next instruction that would
have been executed if the interrupt request had not occurred.     0x0013 External 1 Interrupt

  If interrupts are not enabled, the interrupt input line         0x001B GPIO Interrupt
activity is ignored by the hardware and program execution
continues as normal. Each interrupt source can be                 0x0023 Radio Interrupt
individually enabled or disabled through the use of an
associated interrupt enable bit in an SFR (IE, EIE, E2IE).        0x002B Clock Management Interrupt (see OSCCALIB)
However, interrupts must first be globally enabled by setting
the EA bit (IE.7) to logic 1 before the individual interrupt      0x0033 Power Management Interrupt
enables are recognized. Setting the EA bit to logic 0 disables
all interrupt sources regardless of the individual                0x003B Timer 0 Interrupt
interrupt-enable settings.
                                                                  0x0043 Timer 1 Interrupt
  If an interrupt input line remains set after the CPU
completes the return-from-interrupt (RETI) instruction,           0x004B Timer 2 Interrupt
a new interrupt request will be generated immediately and
the CPU will re-enter the ISR after completion of the next        0x0053 SPI 0 Interrupt
instruction.
                                                                  0x005B UART 0 Interrupt
Interrupt Priority
  Each interrupt source can be individually programmed to         0x0063 UART 1 Interrupt

one of two priority levels: low or high. A low priority           0x006B GPADC Interrupt
interrupt service routine can be preempted by a high priority
interrupt. A high priority interrupt cannot be preempted.         0x0073 DMA Interrupt
Each interrupt has an associated interrupt priority bit in an
SFR (IP, EIP, E2IP) used to configure its priority level. Low     0x007B Output Compare 0 Interrupt
priority is the default. If two interrupts are recognized
simultaneously, the interrupt with the higher priority is         0x0083 Output Compare 1 Interrupt
serviced first. If both interrupts have the same priority level,
a fixed priority order is used to arbitrate.                      0x008B Input Capture 0 Interrupt

Interrupt Latency                                                 0x0093 Input Capture 1 Interrupt
  Interrupts response time depends on the state of the CPU
                                                                  0x009B Random Number Generator Interrupt
when the interrupt occurs. Pending interrupts are sampled
and priority decoded each system clock cycle. Therefore, the      0x00A3 AES Interrupt
fastest possible response time is 5 clock cycles: 1 clock cycle
to detect the interrupt,and 4 clock cycles to complete the        0x00AB DebugLink Interrupt
LCALL to the ISR.

  If the CPU is executing an ISR for an interrupt with equal
or higher priority, the new interrupt will not be serviced until
the current ISR completes, including the RETI and
following instruction.

www.onsemi.com

ADDRESS SPACE                                                    upper half of it may only be accessed by indirect moves
                                                                 MOV @Rx. SFR space can be accessed by direct MOV
  The AX8052 uses a Harvard architecture with 3.5 address        instructions. X space can be accessed by MOVX
spaces. P space is used by instruction fetch and can be          instructions.
accessed using MOVC instructions. I space can be accessed
by direct MOV and indirect MOV @Rx instructions. The

  XREG are the AX8052 registers that do not fit into SFR           The FLASH is organized as 64 1 kByte pages. FLASH
space. The XREG memory map can be found in chapter:              may be erased page-wise and written in 16 Bit words. The
"Register Address Map". The SFR memory map can be                last FLASH page is reserved for factory calibration data and
found in chapter: "SFR Address Map". RREG are the                should not be overwritten. It is highly recommended to call
registers of the radio chip. RREG (nb) is a mirror of the radio  flash_apply_calibration() from libmf early in the startup

FLASH                                                          Features

  The FLASH is the user rewritable non-volatile memory.        · The FLASH Size is 64 kBytes
It is organized as 64 1 kByte pages. It may be erased          · Word Size is 16 Bits
page-wise, and written as 16 Bit words. The small sector       · Erase Sector Size is 1 kByte
size enables the FLASH to be used for configuration data       · Secure Erase Ensures That the Main Flash Data is Fully
where traditionally E2PROM would have been used,
obviating the need for additional E2PROM.                         Erased Before Erasing the Protect and Key Bits

Register: NVADDR0, NVADDR1

Table 21. NVADDR0, NVADDR1

Name             Bits       R/W  Reset                              Description
                                 0x0000
NVADDR           15:0       RW           Flash Address Register

  This register stores the address for FLASH write or page
erase operations.

Register: NVDATA0, NVDATA1

Table 22. NVDATA0, NVDATA1

Name             Bits       R/W  Reset                              Description
                                 0×0000
NVDATA           15:0       RW           Flash Data Register

This register stores the data for FLASH write operations.

Register: NVSTATUS

Table 23. NVSTATUS

Name             Bits       R/W  Reset                              Description

NVBUSY              0       R    -       Indicates the Flash Controller is Busy. This bit can only be observed when

                                         executing from memory other than Flash

                                         been successfully written to the NVKEY register

NVCMD               7:0     W    -       Flash Controller Commands

                                         Command                    Meaning

                                         0×00                       NOP
                                         0×10                       Bulk Erase
                                         0×20                       Flash Page Erase
                                         0×30                       Flash Word Write
                                         0×34                       Flash Protect Bits Write

  The NVSTATUS register reports FLASH controller status
when read and serves as a command register when written.

CACHE AND PREFETCH                                              must be manually flushed. The replacement strategy is
                                                                pseudo-LRU.
  AX8052 contains a small, 4 Words × 16 Bits fully
associative write-through cache to hide the FLASH access          The cache also contains the prefetch controller.
latencies. The cache is consistent with respect to writes over  Prefetching hides memory latencies for streaming accesses
the code bus (MOVC), i.e. a write that hits in the cache        (i.e. program fetching without jumps). Prefetching may be
invalidates the respective cache line. The cache is not         separately enabled/disabled for code fetches and MOVC
consistent with writes to the code memories over other          reads.
interfaces, especially the FLASH using the NV controller,
and to XRAM via the XDATA bus. In this case, the cache

Register: CODECONFIG

Table 25. NVKEY

       Name      Bits    R/W  Reset                             Description

MBZ                   0  RW   0      Must be zero

MBZ                   1  RW   0      Must be zero

MBZ                   2  RW   0      Must be zero

XRAML8                3  RW   0      Enable XRAM in code address space 0×0000-1×1FFF

INVLD                 4  W    -      Writing this bit as 1 invalidates the cache

PREFETCHMOVC          5  RW   0      Enable Code Memory MOVC Prefetching

PREFETCHINSN          6  RW   1      Enable Code Memory Instruction Prefetching

CACHE                 7  RW   1      Enable Code Memory Caching

  The XRAML8 bit maps, if set, the 8 kBytes XRAM into
code memory space. This allows code to execute from
XRAM.

RAM

  AX8052 contains 256 Bytes of IRAM and 8 kBytes of
XRAM. The 8 kBytes XRAM are split into two 4 kBytes
halves. Both halves can be individually preserved or
switched off during sleep mode (refer to the PCON register).
The XRAM memory can be accessed in a cyclesteal fashion
by the DMA controller and the AES crypto engine.

  The maximum value of kFILT, that results in quickest                                                (eq. 1)
calibration (single cycle), but no jitter suppression, is:

                    kFILT + PRESCALER @ 220 f + 512000Hz @ PRESCALER @ 220 REF @ tbase @ kLPOSC fREF

  Smaller values of kFILT result in longer calibration, but
increased jitter suppression.

RADIO INTERFACE                                                  Features

  The Radio Interface is a dedicated interface unit to Axsem     · Directly Maps Radio Chip Registers Into the X Bus
Radio chips, as well as some other SPI slave devices. It
features easy microcontroller access by mapping the Radio           Address Space
registers into X address space. Normally, 8 bit Register
accesses are performed. The Radio Interface however may          · Non-blocking Access Mode May be Used to Hide the
perform up to 32 bit Register accesses, needed with some
Axsem Radio chips to atomically read some tracking                  Access Latency
registers; in this case, the top most byte is returned from the
X address space access, the other data bytes may afterwards      Direct Access via X-Space
be read out from SFR registers.                                    When direct accesses are performed in the Radio

                                                                 Controller dedicated X address space, the controller
                                                                 performs the following actions:

Table 66. DIRECT ACCESS VIA X-SPACE

RREG       R 1. Stall CPU core until the Radio Controller is not busy
4000-4FFF        2. Copy Address Bits 11:0 into RADIOADDR1,RADIOADDR0 (11:0)
                 3. Perform Radio Register Read access
                 4. End CPU core access, return contents RADIODATA3

           W 1. Stall CPU core until the Radio Controller is not busy
                 2. Copy Address Bits 11:0 into RADIOADDR1,RADIOADDR0 (11:0)
                 3. Write CPU data to RADIODATA3
                 4. Perform Radio Register Write access
                 5. End CPU core access

RREG (nb)  R 1. Stall CPU core until the Radio Controller is not busy
5000-5FFF        2. Copy Address Bits 11:0 into RADIOADDR1,RADIOADDR0 (1:0)
                 3. Start Radio Register Read access
                 4. End CPU core access, return data undefined

           W 1. Stall CPU core until the Radio Controller is not busy
                 2. Copy Address Bits 11:0 into RADIOADDR1,RADIOADDR0 (11:0)
                 3. Write CPU data to RADIODATA3
                 4. Start Radio Register Write access
                 5. End CPU core access

  The RREG area is blocking; the CPU is stalled until the        software is then responsible for polling the RCBUSY bit in
register access is terminated. The RREG (nb) area is             RADIOACC and potentially retrieving the data from
non-blocking. The register access is only initiated. The         RADIODATA3.

  The ADC controller supports up to 4 channels. A channel     ADCCLKSRC 2:0 RW        0000         Clock Source
is a combination of multiplexer, single ended/differential,
and gain settings. Each channel has its own result register.                             -   Bits Meaning
When triggered, the ADC converts all configured channels
in sequence. If more than 4 channels are needed, software                                    000 FRCOSC
may first convert a group of 4 channels, read the result,                                    001 LPOSC
reprogram the channel config registers, convert the next                                     010 XOSC
group of 4 signals, and so on.                                                               011 LPXOSC

SPI MASTER/SLAVE INTERFACE                     AND9349/D

                                                              The SPI interface provides a general purpose SPI master
                                                            or slave. Figure 15 shows the block diagram of the SPI
                                                            interface. Its fully programmable, flexible clocking scheme
                                                            allows it to connect to any SPI compatible peripheral or
                                                            master.

                                                             Features

                                                         · 8-bit
                                                         · Master
                                                         · 3 and 4 wire Slave
                                                         · In Master mode, SCLK Can be the System Clock, any

                                                               of the Oscillators or Divided Versions of it

                                                         · Programmable Clock Phase and Inversion

TIME COUNTER 0/1/2

          Figure 17. Timer Block Diagram                        The 16 bit Timer Counter peripheral provides the
                                                              microcontroller with timing. Figure 17 shows the block
                                                              diagram of the Timers. It can also interface to the analog
                                                              world with its SD feature. PWM may be realized together
                                                              with an output compare block. Input signal Timing may be
                                                              captured together with an input capture block.

                                                              Features

                                                              · Supports the Following Modes

                                                                  Timer
                                                                  Pre-Scaler
                                                                  PWM
                                                                  SD
                                                                  Input Capture

                                                              · Can Operate from the System Clock or Another

                                                                 Asynchronous Clock (Note that Some Modes are not
                                                                 Supported with Asynchronous Clock)

                                                              · Provides UART Baud Rate and ADC Sampling Rate

                                                                 Clocks

UART 0/1                                                · Arbitrary Baud Rates can be Generated Using a Timer

  The UARTs provide two Universal Asynchronous             as Baud Rate Generator
Receiver Transmitters.
                                                        · Parity Generation: None, Even, Odd (Software)
Features                                                · Break Detection
                                                        · Optional Receiver Deglitching for Improved Noise
· Standard Universal Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter
· Word Lengths: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 bits                         Immunity
· Stop Bits: 1, 2 (Note that this Only Affects the

   Transmitter, the Receiver will Always Accept
   1 Stop bit)

U0BRKIE           5     RW 0 Receiver Break detect change interrupt enable (interrupt is activated if U0BRKDET changes, and cleared when U0BRKDET is read)
